hypotheses.name: Two-sided directional texture-covariance boundary
hypotheses.physical_signature: Estimate directional semivariogram/covariance on opposite sides of a candidate boundary after side-specific mean removal; seek a repeatable cross-boundary correlation-length or anisotropy discontinuity rather than a large amplitude edge.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue-missing_faults: A fractured or altered damage zone can change spatial texture and directional continuity even when broad magnetic or conductivity amplitudes cancel or the surface scarp is weak. This is a mechanism to test, not an established fault detector.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Depositional facies boundaries, intrusive contacts, map-unit changes, survey leveling seams, and raster resampling can also change covariance.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: A code inventory found existing gradient/edge-coherence, Hessian/vesselness, texture/context classifiers, and endpoint/graph methods, but no two-sided directional semivariogram or covariance-change operator. It differs from raw edge magnitude and Frangi ridge strength.
hypotheses.expected_improvement: Unknown; highest actionable qualitative priority because it is complementary in form and requires no new external layer. Not a numeric prediction.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high (directional neighborhoods and boundary-side controls; reuse the cached numerical stack).
hypotheses.data_requirement: Existing competition bands only; restore the pinned cache and shared evaluator first.
hypotheses.data_obtainability: No new external dataset is required. The current checkout lacks the materialized feature cache; its exact pinned restoration and full preflight remain blocked.
hypotheses.status: UNTESTED; NOT AUTHORIZED FOR RUN in this checkout

hypotheses.name: Spatially cross-fitted conductivity residual margins
hypotheses.physical_signature: Cross-fit a label-free, spatially blocked conditional-quantile model for surface conductivity from basement-depth and terrain context; identify coherent positive/negative residual margins, then test their association with withheld whole-fault segments.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue-missing_faults: Fluid alteration or clay-rich damage adjacent to a buried conduit could be locally unusual after accounting for basin/depth context, revealing a fault-related contrast missed by a catalogue emphasizing mapped surface traces. This does not establish that the conductivity-depth layer is basement thickness.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Saline groundwater, lacustrine clay, irrigation return flow, and changing EM investigation depth can create residual conductivity anomalies.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The repository contains raw conductivity, clay-cap margins and conductivity interactions, but its source hypothesis inventory reports no cross-fitted conditional-quantile residual operator. This is distinct from multiplying conductivity by dilation or scoring the raw conductivity edge.
hypotheses.expected_improvement: Unknown; plausible but more confounded than S26-TCB. Not a numeric prediction.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium (spatial cross-fitting and residual diagnostics; reuse the cached numerical stack).
hypotheses.data_requirement: Existing competition bands only; restore the pinned cache and shared evaluator first.
hypotheses.data_obtainability: No new external dataset is required. The current checkout lacks the materialized feature cache; its exact pinned restoration and full preflight remain blocked.
hypotheses.status: UNTESTED; NOT AUTHORIZED FOR RUN in this checkout

hypotheses.name: Residual heat-flow and shallow-temperature conjunction
layers: USGS Great Basin well heat-flow residuals
hypotheses.physical_signature: Require a candidate corridor to intersect a spatially supported positive heat-flow residual and an independent 2 m temperature anomaly; do not emit from either thermal channel alone.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue-missing_faults: A buried fluid conduit can support shallow thermal expression without a mapped Quaternary scarp. A thermal signal is only corroborating evidence and cannot by itself identify a fault.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Groundwater discharge, warm aquifers, uneven well/probe sampling, and non-tectonic hydrothermal circulation.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The repo has separate heat-flow/Euler and well/spring geothermometer/radiometric work; the proposed conjunction requires an official well heat-flow residual plus independent 2 m probes and a candidate corridor, not just one thermal layer.
hypotheses.expected_improvement: Potentially complementary, but unknown and not ranked as actionable because current raw bytes are absent. Not a numeric prediction.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High (external schema, spatial uncertainty, sampling-density controls, and cross-source provenance).
hypotheses.data_requirement: New external layers: USGS ScienceBase heat-flow item and GDR #1391 2 m probe archive.
hypotheses.data_obtainability: NOT OBTAINABLE IN THIS RUNTIME: previous dated repository records describe runner downloads, but the source bytes are not in this checkout and ScienceBase/GDR hosts are outside the runtime's permitted outbound hosts. Historical availability is not current local availability.
hypotheses.status: UNTESTED; NOT VIABLE FOR CURRENT HOLDOUT RUN

hypotheses.name: Drainage-network displacement and knickpoint trains
layers: existing LiDAR terrain descriptors for contrast
hypotheses.physical_signature: Map channel offsets, beheaded channels, wind gaps, and aligned knickpoint trains; only test anomalies where independent lineament evidence predicts a crossing, using spatially blocked holdout segments.
hypotheses.why_it_may_find_catalogue-missing_faults: Drainage geometry can preserve evidence of displacement after low-relief scarps have been diffused or obscured by basin fill; it is not direct evidence of geothermal activity.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic resistance contrasts, landslides, artificial channels, roads/culverts, and DEM artifacts.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: Prior LiDAR operators primarily score terrain amplitude/roughness/openness/step features. A flow-routing and channel-network topology operator is not present in the current proposal inventory; it must be rechecked against source before implementation.
hypotheses.expected_improvement: Unknown; plausible morphological complementarity, discounted by severe data and processing costs. Not a numeric prediction.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Very high (large tile acquisition, hydrologic preprocessing, stream-network quality control).
hypotheses.data_requirement: New official USGS 3DEP 1 m DEM tiles linked by the challenge DEM table.
hypotheses.data_obtainability: NOT OBTAINABLE IN THIS RUNTIME: source tiles are not present in this checkout, and USGS hosts are outside the runtime's permitted outbound hosts. The official collection page does not establish coverage or availability of the challenge-specific tiles.
hypotheses.status: UNTESTED; NOT VIABLE FOR CURRENT HOLDOUT RUN
